newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel dips on crude, IPE fall.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel dips on crude, IPE fall.

text.p: Singapore physical gas oil market was steady to marginally weaker on Monday, along with the fall in crude and gas oil futures prices in London, traders said.
Gas oil swaps plunged 75 cents with February last quoted at $25.00/$25.10 a barrel. Traders said a $4.25 a tonne plunge in early IPE gas oil futures trading added to the bearish sentiment in Asia.

Physical gas oil was also offered lower by a Singapore trader at $24.80 a barrel for Feb 18-22 lifting fob, from Friday's trade at $25.30. A bid was seen at $24.80, traders said. Another offer was seen at $25.60 a barrel.
Traders said the distressed cargoes off southern China, at least two of which were forced to return to Singapore as buyers refused to accept them, would continue to pressure the market.
Gas oil demand in March has emerged from Nepal which has issued a tender to buy 30,000 tonnes for March 11-20 delivery. Nepal is also seeking kerosene for March 1-10/March 21-31.
Jet fuel continued to get strength from low supplies. Stocks would only be healthy from early March, traders said.

Traders said a South Korean refiner that has sold at least two jet fuel cargoes to the U.S. West Coast was said to have sold another cargo to a Japanese refiner at around $2.00 per barrel above Singapore spot quotes for end arrival in early March, c-and-f.
Traders said there is still demand for jet fuel from the US West Coast but high freight rates are keeping East Asian cargoes away.
A trader bid for 100,000 barrels of jet fuel for feb 18-22 at $31.30, the same level as the highest bid on Friday. An offer was seen at that level.
